name: Spartronics
old_description: In Watertown, South Dakota, Spartronics manufactures complex electronic and electromechanical products for medical, life science, aerospace, and instrumentation and control applications for FDA-regulated, mission-critical, and high-cost-of-failure industrial environments. We partner with our customers along the entire manufacturing value chain, providing engineering, prototyping, manufacturing, test engineering, supply chain management and aftermarket services.
about:
Spartronics operates a 100,000-square-foot electromechanical manufacturing facility in Watertown, South Dakota. The company provides contract manufacturing services for complex electronic and electromechanical products across regulated industries.

The facility specializes in printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) using surface-mount, through-hole, and flex-circuit technologies, along with electromechanical sub-assembly and full box-build integration. Capabilities include automated optical inspection, X-ray inspection, flying-probe and in-circuit testing, environmental stress screening, conformal coating, and functional test development. The site supports new product introduction (NPI), prototyping, and volume production, backed by supply chain management and aftermarket services such as repair, refurbishment, and obsolescence management.

Spartronics serves medical device, life sciences, instrumentation and control, commercial aerospace, defense, and space sectors. Customers include original equipment manufacturers requiring FDA-registered, ISO 13485-certified production for devices such as cardiovascular monitors, neuroablation systems, patient-warming equipment, and RF audio transmission modules. The company also supports aerospace and defense programs requiring AS9100 and ITAR compliance.

The company emphasizes a holistic product ownership mentality, combining in-house PCBA and top-level assembly under one roof. Its quality system adheres to standards including ISO 9001:2015, ISO 13485:2016, AS9100, IEC 60601-1, and IPC-A-610 Class III, with dedicated project managers and cross-functional teams for each program.
